messages:
emma: quick ping — staging batch job intermittently fails with KMS decrypt errors. seems like the SA isn't getting the KMS grant fast enough after a helm deploy. any quick ideas?

emma: terraform snippet i'm applying (simplified):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "batch_irsa_role" {
  name = "batch-irsa-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "batch_key" {
  description = "batch job key"
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "batch_grant" {
  name            = "batch-grant"
  key_id          = aws_kms_key.batch_key.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.batch_irsa_role.arn
  operations      = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

emma: Helm chart creates the k8s ServiceAccount with annotation via values: `serviceAccount.annotations: {"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn": "${aws_iam_role.batch_irsa_role.arn}"}` — but helm install and terraform run in parallel in CI, so sometimes the grant tries to reference the role before kube's SA exists or vice-versa.

leo: do we see the grant failing in aws logs or just decrypt errors in the pod?

emma: pods show `AccessDeniedException: user is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt`. CloudTrail shows the grant exists but principal mismatches the actual role/session ARN used by the pod (session name includes svcacct name+random).

priya: common pattern: two races — 1) IAM role exists but SA annotation not applied so IRSA doesn't get sts:AssumeRole, and 2) grant created referencing role ARN but the assume-role session names differ so key policy/grant principal doesn't match.

jordan: short fix options: 1) create the k8s SA (kubectl/terraform kubernetes_manifest) ahead of helm so the annotation is stable, 2) make the KMS grant refer to the role's canonical principal (aws_iam_role.role.arn) and use a key policy that allows sts:AssumeRole sessions, 3) add a small retry/wait in CI before running terraform that creates the grant.

priya: another approach — do the IRSA role + trust/assume setup in one terraform pipeline, then have helm only annotate the SA with the role ARN (helm should be allowed to create SA). If helm creates SA later, run a lightweight patch: `kubectl patch sa -n ns my-sa -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::123456:role/batch-irsa"}}}'` as a post-deploy step.

leo: if we keep the grant resource, ensure the grantee_principal matches the role session principal pattern. Some folks prefer key policy (allow role ARN) + no grant — fewer moving pieces.

emma: trying a quick patch: add a `local-exec` null_resource that waits for SA annotation before creating grant. pseudo: 
```hcl
resource "null_resource" "wait_sa_annotation" {
  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<-EOT
      for i in {1..12}; do
        if kubectl get sa batch-worker -n staging -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks\\.amazonaws\\.com/role-arn}'; then
          exit 0
        fi
        sleep 5
      done
      exit 1
    EOT
  }
  triggers = { sa = timestamp() }
}
resource "aws_kms_grant" "batch_grant" {
  depends_on = [null_resource.wait_sa_annotation]
  ...
}
```

emma: quick test plan: i'll try patching CI to run helm -> wait for SA -> terraform apply grants. if it works i'll follow up.

infra-bot: CI pipeline #4521: helm upgrade --install batch-worker (staging) succeeded in 28s.

infra-bot: CI pipeline #4522: terraform apply (grants) failed "grantee_principal not found" — will retry in 10s.

jordan: if the null_resource approach works, long-term we should move toward a single orchestration—either helm_release with terraform provider for helm or a small operator that ensures the annotation is present before workloads run.

priya: also document this pattern in infra runbook: "IRSA + KMS grants: order of operations and mitigation steps" so others don't hit the same CI flakiness.

emma: thanks all — testing now, will post results. :thumbsup:
